Population increased in Sheffield

The estimated population of Sheffield in 2024 was 582,493 usual residents, a rise of 1.2% since 2023.

This meant that Sheffield's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Sheffield increased by 4.9%.

Over this slightly longer period, Sheffield was also among the 20% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Sheffield

The average (median) age fell to 36.6 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Sheffield has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Sheffield is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Sheffield's population of 582,493 usual residents was made up of:

  • 103,131 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.7%)
  • 381,601 people aged 16 to 64 years, (65.5%)
  • 97,761 people aged 65 years and over, (16.8%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Sheffield has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (65.5% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Sheffield, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Sheffield
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Sheffield, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 436 people (0.1%). In total, there were 5,670 births and 5,234 deaths in Sheffield.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 4,712 (-0.8%). There were 32,842 people entering the area and 37,554 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Sheffield's population of 11,185 (1.9%) as a result of 18,723 people entering the area and 7,538 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Sheffield was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Sheffield in mid-2023 is 575,586.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 1,645 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 689 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 2,334 people.
